identificationModule.briefTitle: Endostatin in Combination With Oxaliplatin and Radiotherapy in Esophageal Cancer Patients.
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Phase II Study of Endostatin in Combination With Oxaliplatin and Radiotherapy in Esophageal Cancer Patients.

descriptionModule.briefSummary: Endostatin inhibits the pro-angiogenic action of basic fibroblast growth factor and vascular endothelial growth factor in esophageal cancer.This study aims at assessing the efficacy and safety of endostatin combined with concurrent chemoradiotherapy with Oxaliplatin in esophageal cancer patients.

armGroups.label: Chemoradiotherapy Arm
armGroups.description: Radiotherapy will be delivered with a daily fraction of 2.0 Gy to a total dose of 60 Gy over 6 weeks. Endostatin will be administered at a dose of 7.5 mg/m2/day concurrent with radiotherapy. Oxaliplatin (135mg/m², d1) will be administered on Day 1 and Day 29 of radiotherapy.

interventions.name: Endostatins
interventions.description: Endostatin will be administered at a dose of 7.5 mg/m2/day concurrent with radiotherapy.

interventions.name: Oxaliplatin
interventions.description: Oxaliplatin (135mg/m², d1) will be administered on Day 1 and Day 29 of radiotherapy.

interventions.name: Radiotherapy
interventions.description: Radiotherapy will be delivered with a daily fraction of 2.0 Gy to a total dose of 60 Gy over 6 weeks.

primaryOutcomes.description: Response rate will be done after 3-4 weeks following the last radiotherapy session.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Acute and late toxicities assessed based on the common toxicity criteria for adverse events version 3.0 (CTCAEv3.0)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Acute and late toxicities will be assessed based on the common toxicity criteria for adverse events version 3.0 (CTCAEv3.0).

Progression-free survival (PFS) will be calculated from the date of chemoradiotherapy initiation to the date of documented failure (local recurrence or metastasis occurrence) or the date of the last follow-up for those remaining.
Overall survival (OS) will be determined as the time (in months) between the first day of therapy and the last follow-up or the date of death.
